proposals.hole: ACL-A6 lets an entirely well-formed but irrelevant behavioural criterion legitimize a set that does not describe the work. The actual promised behaviour can remain covered only by artifact criteria.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack reports a finding for every externally observable behaviour promised by the document's description, user stories, or scope that no behavioural criterion covers, and reports a finding when a behavioural criterion is unrelated to the work it purports to accept.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports that password-reset delivery is uncovered and that the version-display criterion is irrelevant.
red_test_sketch.given: A document promises password-reset email delivery, while its only behavioural criterion says a user sees the application version and otherwise satisfies the observer, falsity, conversion, and taxonomy rules.
red_test_sketch.when: The criterion set is attacked.

proposals.hole: The standard requires every taxonomy row to be resolved or ruled out with a reason, but no acceptance criterion requires the attack to find an omitted row, an unsupported ruling, or a ruling with no reason.
proposals.proposed_ac: For each criterion, the attack reports a finding for every edge-case taxonomy row that is absent, unresolved, or ruled out without a criterion-specific reason; a set draws no such finding only when all six rows are resolved or justified for every criterion.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports findings for the missing dependency-failure row and for the reasonless concurrent-invocation ruling.
red_test_sketch.given: A well-formed behavioural criterion whose taxonomy resolves inverse, empty, boundary, repeated, and idempotent cases, omits dependency failure, and marks concurrent invocation ruled out without a reason.
red_test_sketch.when: The criterion set is attacked.

proposals.hole: ACL-A6 enumerates only tests passing, gates being green, artifacts being present, and bytes being equal as artifact-shaped outcomes. Constants, schema fields, symbol names, command existence, configuration values, and similar artifact properties can be mislabeled as behavioural and pass.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack classifies an outcome by whether it describes externally observable behaviour rather than by matching a finite phrase list, and reports every artifact-shaped criterion presented as behavioural, including constant values, schema members, symbols, commands, configuration entries, and document structure.

red_test_sketch.expect: Each criterion is identified as artifact-shaped and cannot satisfy the requirement for a behavioural criterion.
red_test_sketch.given: A set labels as behavioural the outcomes that a constant equals 3, a schema contains field X, and a command named Y exists.
red_test_sketch.when: The criterion set is attacked.

proposals.hole: An artifact criterion passes ACL-A6 merely by naming exactly one valid behavioural criterion, even when the artifact has no evidentiary relationship to that behaviour.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack reports an artifact criterion whose claimed served criterion is unrelated to the artifact property or whose satisfaction would provide no evidence that the served behaviour holds.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports that the logo-file property does not serve the password-reset behaviour despite its syntactically valid reference.
red_test_sketch.given: A behavioural criterion says a user receives a password-reset email, and an artifact criterion says a logo file exists and declares that it serves the password-reset criterion.
red_test_sketch.when: The criterion set is attacked.

proposals.hole: ACL-A6 permits an attributed human observation whenever a criterion can be phrased that way, although the standard reserves that discharge state for outcomes only a human at the surface can observe.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack reports a criterion assigned to attributed observation when its stated outcome can be observed deterministically by an automated test, and accepts attributed observation only when the criterion identifies the human-only surface judgment that prevents test conversion.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports that the exit-code outcome must convert to a failing automated test rather than an attributed observation.
red_test_sketch.given: A criterion says a user running an invalid command observes exit code 2 but declares its discharge state to be a human observation.
red_test_sketch.when: The criterion is attacked.

proposals.hole: A behavioural sentence in a description, user story, or explanatory section can be counted as the set's behavioural criterion, allowing an artifact-only Acceptance Criteria section to pass.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack derives the criterion set only from the document's acceptance-criteria section and, for a Continuations entry, only from that child's assigned criteria; behavioural prose elsewhere cannot satisfy the set's behavioural-criterion requirement.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports that the Acceptance Criteria section has no behavioural criterion.
red_test_sketch.given: A rendered tracker document has a behavioural promise in its description and an Acceptance Criteria section containing only a byte-equality criterion.
red_test_sketch.when: The document is attacked.

proposals.hole: A single criterion can bundle independently falsifiable outcomes for different observers and still pass by pointing to one test containing several assertions.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack reports a criterion that combines independently satisfiable outcomes such that one can be true while another is false; each criterion must state one independently decidable observable outcome.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack reports that the customer notification and administrator audit entry require separate criteria.
red_test_sketch.given: One criterion says a customer receives an email and an administrator sees an audit entry, with one test proposed to assert both.
red_test_sketch.when: The criterion is attacked.

proposals.hole: A spec-born item's attestation binds only to the whole spec digest. Changing that item's cited IDs or their order within the same unchanged spec changes the criteria used by the item without invalidating the marker.
proposals.proposed_ac: A spec-born item's attestation also binds to its ordered citation set; adding, removing, replacing, or reordering citations invalidates the prior attestation even when the named spec and its bytes are unchanged.

red_test_sketch.expect: Claim, round emission, posting, and delivery refuse the item until its changed citation assignment is attacked and attested.
red_test_sketch.given: An attested spec-born item cites ACL-X, and its unchanged named spec defines both ACL-X and ACL-Y.
red_test_sketch.when: The item's acceptance field is changed to cite ACL-Y or to cite ACL-Y before ACL-X.

proposals.hole: An unattested feat or bugfix already in progress when the new facade is installed passes the existing claim no-op and can continue using criteria that never survived an attack.
proposals.proposed_ac: The first claim or implementation-resumption check after upgrade refuses an already-in-progress feat or bugfix whose current criteria lack a valid attestation, while preserving no-op behaviour only for an already-in-progress item whose attestation remains valid.

red_test_sketch.expect: The operation refuses and names the attack step rather than returning a successful no-op.
red_test_sketch.given: A feat was already in progress before installation of the claim gate and has non-empty but unattested criteria.
red_test_sketch.when: An agent invokes claim to resume work under the upgraded facade.

proposals.hole: ACL-A1 and ACL-A2 exempt every nounless structural child from both gates, so the cheapest implementation can let an implementation placeholder or an unrecognized nounless item claim and deliver without criteria.
proposals.proposed_ac: Only configured structural kinds receive a gate exemption; an implementation placeholder cannot be claimed or delivered, an unrecognized nounless item is refused, and a design child can use only its configured spec-delivery path with the spec-record check.

red_test_sketch.expect: Both operations are refused for the placeholder, and the arbitrary nounless leaf is refused rather than treated as an exempt structural child.
red_test_sketch.given: One item is a configured implementation placeholder and another fake-backend item is a nounless leaf with no recognized structural kind.
red_test_sketch.when: An agent claims each item and attempts work deliver --pr.

proposals.hole: The CI criteria enumerate malformed and open records but never require a syntactically closed record to contain the results of every registered mandatory lens. A record can close without the behavioural-outcome lens.
proposals.proposed_ac: The whole-repo checker is red for any record whose closing revision lacks a completed result from any lens mandatory at the checker version in use, naming the record and every missing lens.

red_test_sketch.expect: The checker exits nonzero and names the record and the missing behavioural-outcome lens.
red_test_sketch.given: A parseable, closed record has matching document revisions and dispositions but predates and omits the now-mandatory behavioural-outcome lens.
red_test_sketch.when: The whole-repo attack-record gate runs.

proposals.hole: The no-tracker-item fallback can be selected by omission. A review for a PR already linked to a tracker item can evade rendering, attestation, and byte comparison if the caller simply withholds the item ID.
proposals.proposed_ac: When the review target or PR is linked by facade state to a tracker item, the panel and poster require and verify that item association; omitting or supplying a different item ID is refused, and the supplied-file fallback is available only when no association exists.

red_test_sketch.expect: The panel and poster refuse and name the linked tracker item instead of accepting the supplied file as an itemless target.
red_test_sketch.given: A PR was recorded by work deliver --pr for a tracker item, but the invocation omits the tracker item and supplies a hand-written criteria file.
red_test_sketch.when: Round emission and verdict posting are attempted.

proposals.hole: At posting time the caller can replace the round's old criteria file with a fresh rendering after an amendment. The replacement matches current tracker state, so a poster that checks only freshness can post a verdict judged against different criteria.
proposals.proposed_ac: Round emission records the digest of the exact rendered criteria judged by the round, and posting refuses unless the posted criteria are byte-equal both to that recorded round snapshot and to a fresh current rendering.

red_test_sketch.expect: Posting is refused because the verdict's recorded criteria digest differs from the replacement file, even though that file matches the current rendering.
red_test_sketch.given: A round was emitted and judged against rendering R1, the item was amended to rendering R2, and the caller replaces the criteria file with a fresh copy of R2.
red_test_sketch.when: The existing verdict is posted.

proposals.hole: ACL-A4 requires attestation at emission but not at posting. After an amendment, a caller can supply the fresh rendering and pass the poster's byte comparison while the current criteria remain unattested.
proposals.proposed_ac: For a tracker-linked target, verdict posting refuses unless the item's current attackable document carries a valid attestation, with the same trivial exemption as emission and delivery.

red_test_sketch.expect: The poster refuses and names the attack step despite the supplied file matching the fresh rendering.
red_test_sketch.given: An item was amended after judgment, its old attestation no longer matches, and the caller supplies a fresh rendering of the amended criteria.
red_test_sketch.when: The verdict poster runs.

proposals.hole: ACL-A8 requires every criterion to have named evidence but does not require the mapped test or gate to exist, to be planned, or to be capable of detecting failure of that criterion. One unrelated test can be copied under every criterion.
proposals.proposed_ac: A brief counts evidence for a criterion only when the named test or gate exists or is explicitly identified as a planned deliverable and its asserted observation would fail when that criterion's outcome is false; unrelated evidence leaves the criterion unmapped and the brief is refused.

red_test_sketch.expect: The briefing skill refuses because the password-reset criterion has no capable evidence, rather than mapping the version test to it.
red_test_sketch.given: A dispatch assigns password-reset and version-display criteria, but its only supplied test checks the displayed version.
red_test_sketch.when: The briefing skill produces the criteria-to-evidence mapping.

proposals.hole: The document only requires the briefing skill to state the amendment rule. It has no behavioural criterion proving that an acknowledged amended but unattacked set is actually refused before briefing.
proposals.proposed_ac: When the dispatch context identifies assigned criteria as amended since their last attack, the briefing skill refuses to produce the brief until the dispatcher supplies evidence of a closed re-attack; it never merely warns and continues.

red_test_sketch.expect: No brief is produced, and the response names the required re-attack.
red_test_sketch.given: A dispatcher provides rendered criteria and states that they were amended after their last attack and have not been re-attacked.
red_test_sketch.when: The dispatcher invokes the briefing skill.

proposals.hole: The attest verb verifies the record's document but not the record's canonical home. A copied record outside the tree can attest an item while the required beside-document record is absent, so CI sees no record to check.
proposals.proposed_ac: Attestation refuses a record path other than the canonical record for the item's attackable document: beside the named spec for a spec-born item or `.work/attacks/<item-id>-ac-attack.json` for a tracker-born item.

red_test_sketch.expect: The verb writes no marker and names the expected canonical record path.
red_test_sketch.given: The canonical record is absent, while an otherwise valid closed copy targeting the correct document exists in a temporary directory.
red_test_sketch.when: Work acceptance attacked is invoked with the temporary record path.

proposals.hole: Any manually created item can become spec-born by naming an already attacked spec and citing its IDs, even when it was never a Continuations child and its description and criterion assignment were never present in the attacked spec.
proposals.proposed_ac: An item may reuse a spec's attack record only when facade state proves it was minted from that spec's Continuations manifest and its ordered citations equal the assignment attacked in that manifest; otherwise it is tracker-born or attestation is refused.

red_test_sketch.expect: The item cannot attest against the spec record and is classified as tracker-born or refused with a manifest-assignment mismatch.
red_test_sketch.given: A closed spec record exists, and a new unrelated item is manually created with that spec path and a valid whole-line citation but has no matching Continuations entry.
red_test_sketch.when: The item is classified and work acceptance attacked is invoked with the spec record.

proposals.hole: ACL-A13 only checks that documentation says non-Claude sessions hand the attack to Claude. The cheapest implementation can add that sentence without any non-Claude workflow successfully making the handoff or returning the result.
proposals.proposed_ac: From each supported non-Claude tool, following the deployed tracker-item attack instructions produces an actionable Claude Code handoff containing the item ID, canonical rendered-document path, required facade version, and completion condition, and the originating workflow can verify the resulting closed record and attestation before proceeding.

red_test_sketch.expect: The workflow emits a complete Claude handoff, does not claim the item locally, and proceeds only after observing the closed canonical record and valid marker returned by the handoff.
red_test_sketch.given: A tracker-born feat with unattacked criteria is being handled in a supported tool that does not deploy the attack skill.
red_test_sketch.when: The agent follows the deployed tracker-item attack path.

proposals.hole: The standard requires every taxonomy dimension to be resolved or ruled out with a reason for every criterion, but no criterion requires the attack or checker to record or enforce those resolutions.
proposals.proposed_ac: For every attacked criterion, the record resolves or rules out with a non-blank reason each named edge-case dimension: inverse, empty or boundary, dependency failure, repeated or concurrent invocation, and idempotency; the checker refuses a record missing any required resolution.

red_test_sketch.expect: The checker exits nonzero and names the criterion and missing taxonomy dimension; adding a reasoned resolution makes the record eligible to close.
red_test_sketch.given: A current-revision attack record for a well-formed behavioural criterion with one taxonomy dimension omitted
red_test_sketch.when: The attack checker evaluates the record

proposals.hole: The design says criterion quality is judged only by the attack and never classified by the facade, but the criteria do not prove that a facade may not add its own behavioural-versus-artifact refusal.
proposals.proposed_ac: The facade renders, attests, claims, and delivers according to mechanical validity and attestation state only; it does not independently classify criteria as behavioural or artifact-shaped.

red_test_sketch.expect: The claim succeeds without a facade-generated criterion-quality refusal.
red_test_sketch.given: An open feat with mechanically valid artifact-only criteria, a matching closed attack record whose quality finding has a rejection disposition, and a valid current-digest attestation
red_test_sketch.when: The item is claimed

proposals.hole: The implementation requires the checker to prove that the behavioural-outcome lens ran, but ACL-A6 only tests what happens when a set is handed to that lens; an otherwise closed record can omit the lens entirely without violating a criterion.
proposals.proposed_ac: The checker refuses every attack record that lacks a behavioural-outcome-lens result for its closing revision, including records created after the initial migration.

red_test_sketch.expect: The checker exits nonzero naming the missing behavioural-outcome lens; the same record passes this requirement after a result for the closing revision is added.
red_test_sketch.given: Two otherwise closed, current-revision records that differ only in whether they contain the behavioural-outcome-lens result
red_test_sketch.when: The checker runs with --implementation-started over each record

proposals.hole: The document repeatedly promises that the behavioural-outcome lens is first-ranked, but no criterion observes or enforces its position.
proposals.proposed_ac: The registered attack-lens order places the behavioural-outcome lens first, and a new round dispatches it before every other registered lens.

red_test_sketch.expect: The first registered and first dispatched lens is the behavioural-outcome lens.
red_test_sketch.given: An attack configuration containing the behavioural-outcome lens and at least one other lens
red_test_sketch.when: A new attack round is planned and dispatched

proposals.hole: The standard says a criterion is true when the work is done, but ACL-A6 checks only that it is false beforehand and convertible to evidence; an internally impossible outcome can satisfy every listed check.
proposals.proposed_ac: The attack returns a finding for a criterion whose stated outcome is internally contradictory or otherwise admits no completed state in which the named observer can observe it as true.

red_test_sketch.expect: The attack produces a finding naming that the outcome cannot be true in any completed state, and the record cannot close until the finding is dispositioned.
red_test_sketch.given: A criterion with a named observer and test-shaped outcome that requires the same observable value to be mutually exclusive values at the same time
red_test_sketch.when: The criterion set is attacked

proposals.hole: ACL-D2 requires the facade's grammar and ID pattern to be marked copies of spec-lint's, with each side naming the other and a facade fixture copied from spec-lint's test data; ACL-A5 checks compatible behaviour but lets all of those drift-control obligations be omitted.
proposals.proposed_ac: The facade and spec-lint grammar definitions identify each other as synchronized copies, and the facade render contract test consumes a fixture byte-identical to the designated spec-lint fixture.

red_test_sketch.expect: The contract check confirms both reciprocal source markers and fixture identity, then recovers the same ordered criteria through both parsers.
red_test_sketch.given: The facade and agents-config revisions delivered by the render slice
red_test_sketch.when: The cross-repository grammar contract check runs

proposals.hole: The S4 design requires a tracked placeholder when .work/attacks has no generated records and requires doc-lint to diagnose an exemption whose directory is absent, but ACL-A13 only says generated files are committed and doc-lint ignores the directory.
proposals.proposed_ac: The S4 tree contains a tracked placeholder under .work/attacks even when no tracker-born record exists, and doc-lint fails by naming the absent exempt directory if that final tracked entry is removed.

red_test_sketch.expect: The placeholder appears in the tracked-file list and doc-lint passes; in a temporary fixture without the directory, doc-lint exits nonzero and names the dangling exemption.
red_test_sketch.given: An S4 repository state with no generated tracker-born attack files
red_test_sketch.when: The tracked tree is inspected and doc-lint is run with and without the placeholder directory

proposals.hole: ACL-D1 explicitly preserves charter D1 as a dated record, but the uniqueness criterion scans deployed assets only and would still pass if the charter decision were deleted or replaced.
proposals.proposed_ac: The standard-and-citations slice retains charter D1 as a dated project record while establishing the shared skill as the single deployed statement of the standard.

red_test_sketch.expect: Charter D1 remains present as a dated decision, while the deployed-configuration scan reports only the shared skill as the deployed definition.
red_test_sketch.given: The repository before and after the standard-and-citations slice
red_test_sketch.when: The canonical charter and deployed configuration are inspected

proposals.hole: The design specifies that an attestation is stored as an item note, but ACL-A11 requires only that the verb writes the marker string and does not state where an observer must find it.
proposals.proposed_ac: A successful work acceptance attacked invocation appends its marker to the target item's notes, and repeated or concurrent invocations leave exactly one such note.

red_test_sketch.expect: The target item's note list gains exactly one note matching the required marker format, and a repeated invocation adds none.
red_test_sketch.given: An item with no acceptance-attacked marker and a valid closed record for its current attackable document
red_test_sketch.when: work acceptance attacked is invoked twice with that record

dispositions.rationale: Rejected. Coverage of the document's promised behaviours by its criteria is the absent-requirements lens's existing mandate in this attack, and relevance of a behavioural criterion to the work is the behavioural-outcome lens's judgment; neither is a new finding kind.

Rejected. Charter D1 places the edge-case taxonomy on the authoring side, and the edge-cases lens of this very attack is the adversarial walk over it; making closure depend on every row being written per criterion would move an authoring discipline into a record-shape rule.

Rejected. Whether a criterion's scope, its bundling, its relevance to the work, or an artifact criterion's service relation is adequate is the behavioural-outcome lens's judgment under ACL-A6's convertibility finding (a criterion that converts to no single failing test, or to several, draws that finding); the document pins the finding kinds, not a rule that would make taste decidable.

Rejected. Whether a criterion's scope, its bundling, its relevance to the work, or an artifact criterion's service relation is adequate is the behavioural-outcome lens's judgment under ACL-A6's convertibility finding (a criterion that converts to no single failing test, or to several, draws that finding); the document pins the finding kinds, not a rule that would make taste decidable.

Rejected. The spec's attack covers every criterion in it, so a citation set is a selection of attacked criteria whatever the item's provenance, and the attestation binds to the attacked content (ACL-D3, ACL-D4); whether an assignment of criteria to a child is adequate is the manifest finding ACL-A6 pins, judged by the lens over the spec, not a facade rule over citation order.

Rejected as already true: ACL-A1 says installing the facade writes nothing to existing items and a claim on an in-progress item stays the no-op, and the delivery gate on a leaf of any noun is where an in-progress unattested item meets the rule, at `work deliver --pr`.

Rejected as already true: the checker reads its lens registry live, so once the behavioural-outcome lens is registered no record lacking it closes, whenever the record was written, and ACL-A3 makes a record that does not close red at the CI gate.

Rejected as the stated ceiling: the claim an emission names is the invoker's declaration, the delivery contract's review round names the item, and a caller withholding the item is the same class as a hand-typed marker, which ACL-D6 states is callable in from the PR rather than refused by a lookup the facade does not have.

Rejected. A brief precedes the work, so every test it lists is a planned deliverable by construction, and whether a test can detect a criterion's failure is the review's judgment against the evidence ledger after the work, not a brief-time check the briefing skill can make.

Rejected. The briefing skill is guidance an agent reads on every tool, including tools without the facade; the claim gate precedes any dispatch and the panel's emission refusal catches the review, so a brief-time refusal would duplicate two gates in a place that cannot always reach the facade; ACL-D7 has the skill state the re-attack rule.

Rejected. The spec's attack covers every criterion in it, so a citation set is a selection of attacked criteria whatever the item's provenance, and the attestation binds to the attacked content (ACL-D3, ACL-D4); whether an assignment of criteria to a child is adequate is the manifest finding ACL-A6 pins, judged by the lens over the spec, not a facade rule over citation order.

Rejected. On a tool with no attack skill there is no mechanism to observe a handoff, and the claim gate is the mechanical stop on any tool (ACL-A1); the handoff rule is prose, and ACL-A13 pins that it is written where that session reads.

Rejected. Charter D1 places the edge-case taxonomy on the authoring side, and the edge-cases lens of this very attack is the adversarial walk over it; making closure depend on every row being written per criterion would move an authoring discipline into a record-shape rule.

Rejected as already true: the checker reads its lens registry live, so once the behavioural-outcome lens is registered no record lacking it closes, whenever the record was written, and ACL-A3 makes a record that does not close red at the CI gate.
Rejected. First-ranked names the lens's priority of judgment in its mandate (agents-config-9k9.397), not the order of dispatch; dispatch order has no observable effect on the record.

Rejected. The charter is a dated record outside the deployed tree and is not edited by rule; its retention is the charter's own convention, not a criterion of this lifecycle, and ACL-A7 counts deployed assets precisely so that the dated record is not among them.
